description:
fz-usm.4 added `TypeExpr::Map` and its resolver arm, but the map type is only
reachable in a `@spec` RETURN position. In a PARAMETER position it is a parse
error.

## Repro (prebuilt target/debug/fz2, verified independently)

    @spec g(%{b: integer}) :: any
    fn g(m), do: m
    fn main(), do: dbg(g(%{b: 2}))

    error[parse/expected-token]: expected `)` after @spec param list, got eof
      --> d.fz:1:27

Return position is fine -- `@spec g(any) :: %{b: integer}` prints `%{:b => 2}`.

## Root cause

`FragmentCursor::collect_type_tokens` (src/compiler2/quoted_function.rs:1501)
increments bracket depth on `Tok::LParen | Tok::LBrack | Tok::LBrace` only. `%{`
lexes as the SINGLE token `Tok::PercentLBrace` (src/parser/lexer.rs:65), so the
open never counts while the closing `}` decrements depth to -1.
`TypeTokenBoundary::stops_before` (:1409) short-circuits on `depth != 0`, so the
terminating `)` is not treated as a boundary; collection runs to EOF and
`expect_rparen` (:1132) fails.

Return position escapes only because `TypeTokenBoundary::TypeBody` stops on
`When | Eof` and would consume to EOF regardless.

## Controls that isolate it

    @spec g({integer, integer}) :: any    works  -- plain LBrace is counted
    @spec g(%P{}) :: any                  works  -- `%Mod{` lexes as three tokens
    @spec g(%{b: integer}, integer)       fails  -- not an arity-1 artifact

Only `%{` breaks. The same depth bug latently affects
`TypeTokenBoundary::SpecInfixOperand` (the `@spec` infix form) and
`TypeTokenBoundary::Constraint` (a `%{...}` inside a `when` constraint) -- both
should be covered by the fix and by tests.

ELIXIR accepts `@spec g(%{atom => integer}) :: :ok` in parameter position. There
is no param/return asymmetry in Elixir typespec syntax.

## Fix

Count `Tok::PercentLBrace` as depth-opening in `collect_type_tokens`. Consider
making the token classification one helper so a future paired-delimiter token
cannot be missed the same way.

## Checks

- The four probes above: param-position map type parses and runs; the struct and
  tuple controls stay green.
- A `when` constraint carrying a `%{...}` type parses.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.

## Provenance

Filed from fz-usm, whose original framing is fully obsolete: there is now ONE
`CONSTRUCTORS` registry (resolve.rs:109) including `map`, so "built-in type
constructors resolved 3 inconsistent ways" and "map is expressible zero ways"
are both false. `:: tuple` was deliberately excluded by the closed fz-usm.6 and
is pinned by two tests, so it is not a gap. `map(k,v)` is the deferred fz-usm.5
decision. This parse bug is the one live defect that survey found.
title: A map type in a @spec parameter position fails to parse: collect_type_tokens does not count PercentLBrace toward bracket depth
